_comment: ngsolve stokes#4 (do not hardcode a direct solver name; 'except RuntimeError: continue' is broken). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, Stokes block matrix on unit_square maxh 0.25 with .Inverse() asked for five names. NgException is confirmed not to be a RuntimeError subclass, on the class itself. On this build sparsecholesky and umfpack succeed; pardiso raises a plain builtins.RuntimeError ('MKL Pardiso is not available'), mumps raises NgException ('MumpsInverse not available'), and a nonexistent name raises NgException naming the input and listing the allowed names. So the same call with only the name changed produces two different exception types. The naive loop is then RUN, over a preference order that puts the optional solvers first as a fallback loop would: it catches pardiso's RuntimeError, continues, and escapes on mumps's NgException. A loop catching Exception picks umfpack, whose answer matches the reference exactly. Mutation: putting sparsecholesky first in the preference order lets the naive loop succeed and the fixture fails on naive_loop_is_broken. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 reorders PREFERENCE to put sparsecholesky -- a solver this build has -- first, so the naive 'except RuntimeError: continue' loop succeeds on its first try and never meets the NgException. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'naive_loop_is_broken=True' and 'chosen_solver_actually_solves=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear, so the fixture goes red. The second removal is itself a finding: once sparsecholesky is the chosen solver, chosen_solver_relative_error is nan, so the 'outcome=ok' recorded in the per-name table means only that .Inverse() did not raise, not that the solver solves this indefinite saddle-point system. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
